entities.name: Primary sclerosing cholangitis
observations: Cholestatic liver tests plus diffuse multifocal beading of intrahepatic and extrahepatic ducts on MRCP is characteristic of large-duct PSC.
After characteristic cholangiographic diagnosis, evaluation for associated inflammatory bowel disease with ileocolonoscopy and biopsies is recommended.
ERCP is generally reserved for therapeutic intervention or evaluation of relevant/indeterminate strictures rather than routine diagnostic confirmation.
Liver biopsy is mainly considered for small-duct PSC or suspected autoimmune hepatitis overlap.

entities.name: Inflammatory bowel disease
observations: PSC is associated with inflammatory bowel disease, including clinically occult colitis; colonoscopy with biopsies is used to evaluate for this association.

entities.name: Colonoscopy
observations: Ileocolonoscopy with biopsies is the most appropriate next test after MRCP demonstrates characteristic PSC, to assess for associated inflammatory bowel disease.
